title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Palindrome via Difference Array
statement:
Given an array A of N positive integers, you want to make it a palindrome. In one operation you can increment or decrement any element by 1 (cost = 1). Find the minimum total cost.

Key observation: for each pair (A[i], A[N-1-i]), the minimum cost to make them equal is |A[i] - A[N-1-i]|. Sum all such pair costs.

**Twist (range query layer):** Before computing, apply Q difference-array range operations. Each operation adds value V to all positions from L to R (1-indexed). Apply these first, then compute the palindrome cost on the modified array.

This combines the Difference Array and simulation topics.
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers N and Q.
Line 2: N space-separated integers A[1..N].
Next Q lines: each contains three integers L, R, and V.
outputFormat: A single integer: the minimum cost to make the modified array a palindrome.

examples.explanation: Array [1,5,3,5,1] is already a palindrome. Cost = 0.

starterCode.python:
n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
diff = [0] * (n + 2)
for _ in range(q):
    l, r, v = map(int, input().split())
    diff[l] += v
    diff[r + 1] -= v
# Apply difference array
cur = 0
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    cur += diff[i]
    a[i - 1] += cur
# Write your solution here: compute minimum palindrome cost
